result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would rewire human empathy—not by forcing it, but by making it effortless to truly understand the lived experience of anyone, anywhere. Not just intellectually, but viscerally: to feel the weight of another’s hunger, the sting of their injustice, the warmth of their joy, as if it were your own.  

Not through magic, but by dissolving the illusions that separate us—borders of nation, race, belief, or circumstance—and revealing, in stark clarity, that every person’s pain and hope are made of the same fragile, urgent stuff as our own.  

Because if we *knew*, undeniably, that the child starving in Yemen, the refugee drowning in the Mediterranean, the neighbor hiding their despair behind a smile—they are *us*… we’d stop building walls. We’d start healing. Not out of charity, but because it would feel as natural as tending to our own wounds.  

The world wouldn’t become perfect overnight. But cruelty, greed, and indifference would lose their camouflage. And that? That would change everything.
